profile.reading:
This is a Credit Suisse data center at 201 Main Avenue in Clifton, Passaic County, New Jersey, part of a corridor of financial services back office and technology facilities that grew up along the northern New Jersey side of the New York metropolitan area over the past several decades. Major Wall Street firms have long favored suburban New Jersey counties such as Passaic, Bergen, and Middlesex for data processing, disaster recovery, and back office operations, since these sites offer lower real estate costs and construction density than Manhattan while still sitting within the short, low latency distance investment banks need for trading and settlement systems, a pattern shared by other bank operated facilities in the same region.

Credit Suisse's ownership of this facility predates a major change in the bank's corporate status. Following a crisis of confidence in the bank's stability, Switzerland's financial regulator FINMA arranged for UBS Group to acquire Credit Suisse in a deal announced on March 19, 2023, with the Swiss National Bank providing liquidity assistance and the Swiss Confederation offering guarantees to complete the transaction and prevent broader damage to Swiss and international financial markets. FINMA's own statement on the deal emphasized that Credit Suisse's business activities, including its accounts, security accounts, and other customer facing services, would continue without restriction or interruption through the transition rather than an abrupt shutdown. Over the following months and into 2024, UBS integrated Credit Suisse's operations into its own corporate and legal entity structure, a process that ultimately absorbed Credit Suisse's Swiss banking subsidiary and its parent holding company into UBS.

No public source establishes the current operational status of this specific Clifton building following that integration process. Whether the site continues to run under Credit Suisse's name, has been folded into UBS's broader technology infrastructure, or has been repurposed or vacated entirely cannot be stated with confidence here. Neither the facility's square footage nor its power capacity in megawatts is publicly disclosed, and no year built has been documented in available records. What can be documented is the address itself and the fact that Credit Suisse, prior to its 2023 to 2024 absorption into UBS, was one of the major global banks maintaining back office and technology infrastructure in the New Jersey suburbs of New York, alongside other financial institutions with similar footprints in the same corridor.

reading.body:
Credit Suisse operates a data center in Clifton, Passaic County, New Jersey that the operator does not publish power capacity or square footage for. The facility appears to be a private corporate data center rather than a marketed colocation or cloud service, and no specification detail is available from the operator's public sources.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities, of which only 5 publish power capacity figures totaling 111.3 megawatts. This Clifton facility ranks sixth in the state by published megawatts, which means it publishes no figure and therefore does not appear in the state's published capacity total.

Without published specifications, this campus cannot be assessed for its role in AI infrastructure. The operator's choice not to disclose power or space figures leaves its relevance to AI scaling unknown.
